description: Put a question to formalised law. When the answer is "not established" it carries whyNot — the engine's why_not report: the candidate rules and the state of every conjunct (satisfied / not satisfied / undetermined); the missing facts are visible there and need not be guessed. BEFORE THE FIRST call obtain the predicate names through law_search (a question in your own words → addresses) or law_packages (the signatures of a known instrument) — an invented name will be rejected. If the tool returned an error or "not established", THAT IS THE ANSWER: pass it to the user and do not substitute general knowledge about the law of some other country. But "I found no suitable instrument" is NOT an answer until law_search has been asked: silence of the catalogue is a property of searching by title, not a conclusion about the corpus. kind='truth' — whether a fact is established; kind='collect' — enumerate the records; kind='deadline' — compute a time limit on the official calendar; kind='positions' — which DUTIES arose from the facts and what their statuses are; kind='why_not' — the why_not report on the same goal, whatever the status of the answer. The answer carries the rules applied, the warnings and the provenance with hashes; truth/collect also carry a signature block for presentation. The server does not guess: where a norm is not formalised, the answer is "not established" or an error.

after.description: deadline: the date of the event

args.description: the arguments of the predicate in the order of its signature; with kind='collect' exactly one of them is the selection variable ?name (for example ['urn:x:water', 'urn:x:mix', '?value']), the rest are values. Values follow the parameter type: an entity — 'urn:…' or a short name; Date — 'YYYY-MM-DD'; Money — '<number> <currency>' ('43250 KZT'); Quantity — '<number> <unit>' with the unit exactly as the package spells it; a constant of the package — its name

calc.description: kind='calc': a tree {op,left,right}, op ∈ add|sub|mul|div|le|lt|ge|gt|eq|ne (the synonyms divide/multiply/plus/minus and the signs are accepted); the leaves are 5 | '3932 KZT' | '2 mrp' | {lookup: 'mrp', args: [2026]} — a statutory value from the corpus; aggregates are {aggregate: 'sum', element: '?v', over: [{predicate, args with '?variables'}]} over the facts given in facts

context.description: Expliziter Zeitkontext: timezone ist ein IANA-Name; decisionTime und knowledgeTime sind vollständige Instants mit UTC oder Offset und werden unverändert übernommen. Mit context ist legalTime erforderlich; ein Profil kann alle Felder verlangen

days.description: deadline: the length of the period

deadlinePolicy.description: the policy for counting time limits expressed in days: the StableId of a deadline policy declared in the world of the question (e.g. 'urn:kz:corpus:clir:administrative-code#AC_WORKING_DAY_TERMS'), or its short name when exactly one declaration carries it. An inline object {start_count: 'same_day'|'next_day', include_end: true|false, roll: 'no_roll'|'next_working_day'|'previous_working_day'[, month_end: 'last_day_of_month']} is accepted only by a 0.1 world; a 0.2 world refuses it, and the refusal names the declared policies. Without a policy a norm carrying a time limit answers MISSING_POLICY — the policy is set by the law of procedure and the server never assumes one. The snapshot of the official calendar for working days is supplied by the server itself whenever an instrument counts them.

evidence.description: case documents, section 74, evidence_item nodes. One document is referenced from provenance.evidence of many facts. payload.confidence is data for the EvidencePolicy; the engine does not evaluate the number

evidencePolicy.description: StableId of an evidence_policy node, section 78.2. Without it, previous calls keep their behaviour. The confidence threshold is a rule of that policy, not an argument of the call

facts.description: facts of the case: [{predicate, args, provenance, negated?, package?, judgment?}]. provenance is required and must be an object; {} is allowed. Its fields are optional: {origin?, evidence?: StableId, span?: {page?, quote?, offset?}, extractor?: {name, version?, confidence?}, observedAt?, recordedAt?}. origin defaults to case_input. evidence and observedAt are not required; the extractor is lowered to was_generated_by and a document to was_derived_from. confidence is a decimal string; the package EvidencePolicy reads the threshold, not the host. package resolves an ambiguous short name; args use the same notation as the args of the question

focused.description: kind='truth': ask as focused_truth — the same answer as the full truth, but the proof and the warnings cover only the cone of the question; the answer carries evaluationKind and the slice hashes (focus); the cone in focus is reduced to coneHash and the predicate count, the full cone manifest comes in evaluation.focusManifest with proof=true. A slice is not an audit document: law_prepare_answer does not accept it for publication

kind.description: the kind of question (truth by default)

package.description: narrow the question to one package of law

proof.description: return the evaluation field with the proof graph in the answer — a ready-made input for law_explain (kind truth|collect; by default a summary without the graph)

responseMode.description: full (default) — the complete answer. compact is accepted for compatibility: this server builds no short reply and returns the same complete answer in both modes; there is no fullAnswer reference and no stored snapshot of the answer.

selectedInterpretations.description: named readings; for an exactly_one group choose exactly one StableId out of law_packages/law_rules

supportEdges.description: support edges, section 75, support_edge nodes: from is the document id, to is the fact literal, relation is supports or refutes. Admission is decided by the package EvidencePolicy, not by the host

version.description: the exact package version pinned by the client (open('name@version')); if it differs from the profile composition the host refuses instead of answering with another version

name: law_ask
